To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cell‐free eukaryotic protein production is a promising alternative to conventional in vivo production systems, and that the described system is a valuable tool for the modification of antibody fragments.
cell‐free eukaryotic expression systems are a promising tool for the production and modification of antibody fragments.
the presented cell‐free expression systems for eukaryotic antibody fragments are a powerful and versatile tool for the rapid and efficient production and engineering of functional scFv fragments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cell‐free production of functional eukaryotic antibody fragments and the development of a versatile platform for their engineering, modification, and labeling.
the development and optimization of a eukaryote‐based cell‐free protein production system, which is able to express functional single‐chain antibodies in vitro.
the production of functional antibody fragments in a eukarya‐based cell‐free expression system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented eukaryotic in vitro translation system is a powerful tool for the production of functional scFvs and for the engineering and modification of these molecules by site‐specific incorporation of noncanonical residues.
the cell‐free system is an efficient tool for the production of scFv molecules, and that it can be further developed into an efficient platform for antibody fragment engineering and modification.
cell‐free eukaryotic protein expression systems are a promising and powerful tool to synthesize, modify, and engineer antibody fragments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell‐free expression in S. frugiperda cell extracts is a promising approach for the production, modification, and engineering of antibody fragments.
cell‐free expression systems based on insect cells are highly efficient and flexible for the production of functional scFv fragments, as well as for the engineering of these antibody fragments.
the described eukaryotic in vitro translation system is a powerful tool for the production and engineering of functional scFv molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

eukaryotic, endotoxin‐ and pathogen‐free cell‐free expression systems are suitable for the production, modification, and engineering of scFvs and that the translocation of scFvs into the lumen space of endogenous microsome vesicles is a promising strategy to increase the functional activity of scFvs.
the Sf21‐based cell‐free translation system is a promising tool for the production, modification, and engineering of functional scFv antibody molecules.
the cell‐free system based on Sf21 cell extract can be used for the production, modification, and site‐specific labeling of scFv molecules.
